Maybe somewhere near the coast, just to get some fresh air and do something different. That sounds nice. I’d love to go away for a bit. It’s been a while since I’ve had a proper holiday.

I've been thinking a lot lately about how things used to be. Back when we had the heating working properly. It's so cold in this house now, and I don’t know how we're going to manage without it for much longer. I know, love. I've been trying to keep the radiators as warm as I can with the electric blankets and all. But it’s not enough, is it? I feel like I’m getting more and more wrapped up in these blankets every night. You know, I’ve got a friend who lives in a flat with central heating and they can’t even imagine living without it. I told them, "You're lucky, you don’t have to worry about the heating being out for days on end." Yeah, I hear you. I remember when the whole country was without power for a few days back in '90 something. It was chaos. I had to use a fire for the first time in my life, and it was terrifying. Oh, I still remember that too. It was so cold, and the dog had to sleep inside with us. I never thought I’d see the day when I'd be worrying about the heating again. I don’t know, love. I think maybe we should start talking about getting some kind of backup generator or something. It’s not like we can just go to the shop and buy a new boiler. That’s a fair point. I think we should all get together and discuss it. We could maybe look into some options. I’ve heard of people using solar panels and all that. I’ve been reading about it too. I think it’s worth a look. But the problem is, we’re all on a tight budget now. I mean, with the cost of living the way it is, it's hard to stretch a pound. Yeah, I know what you mean. I remember when the cost of living was nothing like it is now. Back then, we could afford a bit more. I suppose we just have to make do. I keep telling myself that we’re not as poor as we think we are. We’ve got our health, our family, and we still have the dog. That’s something, isn’t it? Absolutely. You know, the dog might be the only thing keeping us sane at this point.

I just watched this film last night, and I still can’t get it out of my head. It was  The Favourite , right? That one with Yalitza Aparicio and Rachel Weisz. You know, the one that’s basically about power and control? Oh yeah! I saw it too. I didn’t know Rachel Weisz was in it. I thought she was more of a romantic comedy star. But I loved it. It was so intense. I couldn’t look away. Isn’t it? I mean, the way they portrayed the characters... like, they were both powerful but also so flawed. It felt like real life. I think it’s one of those movies that you have to watch more than once to really get it. Definitely. I feel like I missed something the first time. I think I was too busy with work. Wait, you’re a conference and events coordinator. How do you manage to find time to watch films? Honestly, I have to plan my time carefully. I’ll often watch one or two films a week, and then I’ll have a short break. But I’ve got to say, I’m not as into movies as I used to be. I’m more into documentaries these days. Though I do still enjoy a good drama. That’s interesting. I’ve been trying to get back into films again after a long break. I think I need to start with some classics. Like, maybe  Casablanca  or  Citizen Kane ? Oh, you should! I think  Citizen Kane  is a bit too slow for some people, but it’s a masterpiece. I remember seeing it at a film club when I was at university. It was so different from anything I’d seen before. I’ve heard so much about it. I just need to find the right time. Speaking of films, are you going to the family gathering next weekend? Yeah, I’m going. It’s my cousin’s birthday. We’re all meeting up in the countryside. I think we’re doing a barbecue and a film night. I’ve already booked the projector and the snacks. Sounds like a great idea. I should come too. It’ll be nice to catch up properly. I’ve been so busy with work that I haven’t seen you in ages. Definitely. I’d love that. Maybe we can even bring a film to show.

I've been thinking a lot about the Scottish referendum, love. It’s a bit of a big deal, isn’t it? I mean, it’s not just about independence—it’s about identity, history, and what it means to be Scottish. Yeah, I guess so. But honestly, I’m not sure what it really means. I mean, I know Scotland’s different from England in a lot of ways, but I don’t think I’d ever want to be part of another country. It feels like we’re already part of the UK, even if we have our own way of doing things. That’s a fair point, but I think it’s more about the people who live there. You know, the sense of being Scottish. I remember growing up in Yorkshire, and even though I’m English, I always felt a bit of a connection to the north of England and Scotland too. Maybe it’s the shared history, the old border towns, the way people talk. I get that. I mean, my gran’s from the Borders, and she always talks about how different it was back then, before the UK was really all one country. But I still don’t see why it matters so much now. I mean, if Scotland is independent, how does it affect us? I mean, we’re already part of the UK, and we still get all the benefits. That’s a good question. But the thing is, the UK is a union of nations, and Scotland has its own voice. If they vote for independence, it could change a lot of things—like the economy, trade, and how much power the Scottish government has. It’s not just about leaving the UK, it’s about what kind of country they want to be. I guess I just don’t see what the big deal is. I mean, I’d rather have the status quo. I don’t think I’d ever want to live in another country. I like being British, and I like where I am. I can see how someone might feel that way. But I think the key is that people should have the right to decide for themselves. It’s a democratic process, and it’s about giving people a voice in their future. I suppose that makes sense. I just need to see more about it, you know?

I swear, I can't understand a word they're saying. It’s like they’re speaking in code or something. Yeah, I know, isn’t it? I think it’s just the way they’re talking. I mean, they sound like they’ve got a lisp or something. I think it’s more about the accent. I’ve heard people from different parts of the country, and it’s like, every area has its own way of speaking. It’s not just a lisp, it’s just how they’re used to talking. Oh, I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to figure out what they’re saying. It’s like they’re dropping some letters or something. Like, “I’ve got a new job” becomes “I’ve got a new job.” D’you know what I mean? Yeah, exactly! It’s like they’re eliding vowels and consonants. Like, "they’re" becomes “they’re” and it’s just not clear to me. I can’t tell if they’re saying “they’re” or “they are.” Yeah, I think that’s called elision. It’s when people drop certain syllables or sounds when they speak. I remember learning about that in English class. It’s common in some accents, especially in northern England, I think. Yeah, I don’t know if it’s just the accent or if it’s the way they’re phrasing things. I mean, when they say “I’ve got a new job,” it sounds like they’re saying “I’ve got a new job.” It’s so frustrating! I think it’s part of the regional dialect. I mean, I’ve heard people from Derby talk like that too. It’s not just the accent, it’s the way they’re used to speaking. It’s like, if you grow up in that area, you just start speaking that way. I remember when I first moved to Chester, I was trying to understand people from Liverpool. It was like a whole different language. I had to ask people to repeat themselves so many times. It was so confusing! Yeah, I can totally relate. I come from Doncaster, so my accent is kind of like theirs. But I still don’t get how people from Chester speak. It’s like they’re saying things in a different way. Maybe that’s why they call it the “Jeremy Kyle” show.

I can't believe the Euros are already halfway through. I’ve been watching every game, but I’ve been so busy with work and my PhD that I haven’t had time to really settle in. Yeah, it’s wild how fast it’s gone. I remember when we were in Sunderland, we’d always have a big TV setup for the Euros. It was like the whole town was in the same room. You’ve got to admit, though, this year’s got some real talent. For sure. I was watching the Belgium match the other night. The way they played—it was like watching a dance. I mean, even the goalkeeper made it look like a ballet. I told my mum, "If they don’t win, I’m going to be so sad." I know what you mean. I feel the same about the Euros. But then again, I was at the Olympics last year. I still can’t get over how amazing that was. I remember when we saw the gold medal ceremony for the team, it was just so emotional. Oh, I was there too! I remember being in the stands, and I swear the atmosphere was electric. It was like the whole country was cheering for them. I even tried to knit a little flag for the team. It turned out more like a weird sock, but I still kept it. That’s a funny story. I did something similar. I tried to knit a little Olympic ring out of wool, but I ended up with a lopsided circle. I still have it in my drawer. I should definitely put it in my thesis as a kind of badge of honor. That’s a great idea! You know, I was actually thinking about baby names the other day. I’m starting to get serious about it now. I was considering “Leo” or “Ethan,” but I’m not sure yet. “Leo” is a solid choice. I think it’s got a nice ring to it. And it’s not too common, which is always a plus. I was thinking about “Oliver” or “Liam.” They’re both strong names but not too overused. Yeah, I like “Leo” too. It’s like a modern classic. I go back and forth between it and “Noah.” But I think I’ll have to settle on one soon. I can’t keep changing my mind like this.

I just watched  The Bee Movie  again with the kids, and I still can’t get over how much it’s about the importance of hard work and community. It’s such a silly movie, but there’s a lot to learn from it. Yeah, it’s funny how the bees are trying so hard to be the best, but then they just want to enjoy life. I mean, isn’t that a bit like being a kid? You work so hard to be the best, but then you just wanna play. I was like, “But why do they want to be the best?” I thought bees just do what they do. They don’t get to choose. Exactly, and that’s what’s so cute. It makes you think about how we, as humans, sometimes put so much pressure on ourselves to be the best. But sometimes, it’s just about being happy and working together. And then there’s all the royal stuff in there. The queen bee is like a monarch, right? It’s kind of like the royal family, isn’t it? Oh, absolutely. The queen bee is the most powerful, and everyone else is just there to support her. It’s like royalty in a way. You know, I was just thinking about that the other day. Shouldn't the UK be a republic instead of a monarchy? Why? I like the Queen. She’s cool. I know, but I think people just want more say in how the country is run. Plus, it’s expensive to keep a royal family around. You know, they have to pay for all their stuff, like the palaces and the fancy stuff. But they also have a lot of good stuff. Like, the royal gardens and all the things they do for charity. Yeah, but do you think that’s worth the cost? And then there’s all the talk about wanting to be royalty. I remember when the kids were younger, they all wanted to be princes or princesses. You know, “I’m going to be the Queen when I grow up!” I wanted to be a king. I thought I would have a big castle and a dragon. That’s so cute. But I think it’s more about wanting to feel important and have a big family, like in the movies. Exactly. And your Grandmother’s old house, that’s like a small palace in its own way.

I just love this café, it's got such a cosy feel. I've been coming here for years, you know. Just the right amount of local charm without being too pretentious. I agree, it's a nice spot. I like the way they’ve kept things simple. I’ve been coming here with my mum more often lately. She’s been saying she wants to clear out her old stuff. Yeah, I heard about that. I remember the old market place and all the stalls. The place had character, you know. It’s a shame that the old buildings are getting knocked down. I think it’s a bit of a loss for the town. But maybe it’s for the best. I mean, not everything has to stay the same. Yeah, but I heard she’s thinking of doing something with the garden. She’s had a lot of twists and turns in life. But she’s still got that spark. Definitely. She’s got such a warm heart. I think she’s just trying to make sure her legacy is something people can enjoy. I hope she makes the right decision. I mean, moving house is a big thing. It’s not just about the house, it’s about the memories. That’s true. I think it’s about finding a place that makes you feel at home again. Exactly. And I think she’s got that somewhere. I just hope she finds it soon. I’m sure she will. And when she does, I’m sure she’ll make it all happen.

I just got a text from my colleague, asking if I can help her with an interview for a Masters in Education. She's been working on her application and needs some advice on how to structure her personal statement. Oh, that's great! I bet you'll be able to help her. You always have such clear ideas about teaching and learning. How did you get into teaching anyway? I mean, it's not something I ever considered. Honestly, it was a bit of a last-minute decision. I was studying English Literature and then got a job teaching English at a local school. I loved it, even though it was tough at first. I mean, I had to adapt to the way students learn and how to keep them engaged. It's not just about knowing the subject, it's about knowing how to teach it. That’s true. I mean, if you're not sure, it's better to take a year to figure it out than to rush into something that doesn’t feel right. Thanks, I really appreciate that. It’s just so much pressure, you know? Between work and planning for the future, it’s hard to find the right balance. I know. That's why I think it's so important to have someone to talk to. You're not alone in this.

So, do you know what’s up with this new music trend? I’ve been seeing so many people on Instagram just blasting this weird synth stuff. It’s like, what even is it? Oh, I know! Deal. I think we’ll be fine. Let’s just go with the plan and see if it works out. Maybe we can even grab some coffee after. I just got a new Pokémon game, and I think it's amazing. I've been playing it all evening. It's got so many new characters and features. That's great! I remember when I was your age, I used to game with my dad all the time.

I just found this old box under the bed. It’s got some of our childhood toys in it. You remember that gardening set we had? The one with the tiny watering can and the little spade? Oh, how I do! That was the best toy ever. We used to make our own little gardens in the back yard with the pebbles and sticks we found. I still have that tiny watering can in the attic, if you ever want to see it. It was such a simple thing, wasn’t it? But it felt like the whole world was in our hands. You remember the Bako building set too? The one that made us think we were building skyscrapers? My word, yes! We used to spend hours putting those together. I think we even built a tower so high, it fell over. You screamed so loud, I was sure the neighbors would come out. I remember that! You were so proud of it. I think the tower was only about two feet tall, but to us, it was the tallest building in the world. Exactly! We used to imagine we were architects, builders, and engineers. I wonder what we’d do with those toys now. I’ve tried to get my granddaughters interested in building things – they’re more into their phones than anything else these days. I know. It’s sad, isn’t it? I think the reason we were so into those toys is because there was nothing else to do. We had to create our own fun. Those toys were our escape. Exactly. It makes me think of how much we’ve changed. I suppose we are lucky we had those things. I mean, not all kids have the chance to play with toys like that. I remember when we had to tidy out the cupboard, we used to get so excited about finding that old box. Yes, it’s like going back in time. I feel like I’m ten years old again, playing with the Bako set and pretending I was building a city. It’s such a beautiful memory. It truly is. I think we should keep those toys. They’re more than just old junk – they’re pieces of our past, and they remind us of how much joy we had growing up. They’re worth keeping. I agree. Let’s put them somewhere safe.

I can't believe it's already mid-July. I swear, the mosquitoes have been relentless all week. We took the baby to the park yesterday, and I was practically wearing a net cover like a tent. Yeah, I know. They’re everywhere. I swear, they’re out to get me. I even tried burning some citronella candles, but I think they just enjoyed the smoke more than the smell. Honestly, I felt like I was in a horror movie. I had to keep swatting them off the baby’s face. Didn’t even want to risk her getting bitten. I mean, I know they’re just bugs, but with a baby, it’s not worth the risk. I get it. I was so worried I’d wake up with a mosquito bite on my neck. But I guess I should be grateful they’re not as bad as they were last summer. Wait, did you hear about that gig we were supposed to play last night? Yeah! That jazz gig at the old venue. I was really looking forward to it. But I guess with the way things are going, traffic’s been a nightmare too. I got stuck in the worst jam on the way home from work the other day. Took me over an hour just to get to the bus stop. I know, it’s been so bad. I swear, every time I try to take the bus, it’s delayed by at least ten minutes. I’ve been considering buying a car. I’d rather take a bus or walk, even if it takes longer. At least I know where I’m going. I think the main thing is that we need to figure out a way to get around without stressing out every day.

I've been thinking about redecorating my flat in Cairo. It’s been a while since I’ve done anything with the walls. I’m starting to feel like I need a bit of a refresh after all this time. It was a bit of a project, but it made a huge difference. Blue’s a safe bet, I suppose. I’ve always liked the calming effect it has. I got a smart thermostat and lighting system, and it’s been a game-changer. The lights adjust to the time of day, and the temperature is better controlled. It saves money in the long run. That’s interesting. I’ve been meaning to look into smart home systems. Some people think it’s a goin’ concern, but I’ve seen plenty of real stories—people who came here, worked hard, and contributed. They’re not the problem. The problem is the system that’s supposed to help them. To the people who still believe in a fair system, then. May we not lose hope. To that. And may we keep our spirits high, even when the world feels like it’s slipping away.

So, do you ever find it funny how people think they know everything about the internet, but they’ve never even used a real library? Oh, it’s getting late. I think I’ll have a cup of tea. Anyone want one? Yeah, I’d love a tea. Thanks, Gran. I’ve been reading about the history of York. You never know, lad. You might find you enjoy it. I did. And it’s a great way to keep your mind sharp. Maybe I’ll try that. I’ve got a bit of an interest in mechanics, to be honest. I just found this old photo of us in London last summer. Do you remember that trip? We were so tired from walking all day, but it was one of those perfect days. Oh yeah! That day at Covent Garden. I just got a call from my cousin in Dublin. She said that my old grandmother is coming to visit us in Hunsonby next week. I can't believe we've got a bin strike again. It's like they're trying to make us go mad. What's the plan? Are we going to just stack the bins in the hallway? I know, it's so frustrating. I can't believe it's already December. I feel like I haven't even had time to properly adjust to the weather, and now it's starting to rain again. So, do you know what’s up with these new plants in the garden? I’ve been trying to grow some herbs, and I’m not even sure if I’m watering them right. You’re doing it wrong, honestly. I just can’t believe how much time I’ve spent thinking about killer whales this week. I mean, it’s not like I’m some kind of marine biologist or anything. I've been thinking about the hostel we were talking about earlier. I reckon we could do with more staff, especially with all the kids coming in these days.
